records.jsonld: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@graph":[{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/hot-water-safety-checks/#webpage","@type":["WebPage","FAQPage"],"breadcrumb":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/hot-water-safety-checks/#breadcrumb"},"description":"Essential hot water safety checks — gas, pressure relief and scald risk — what you can check yourself and what needs a licensed plumber. A clear guide.","image":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/hot-water-safety-checks/#primaryimage"},"inLanguage":"en-AU","isPartOf":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/#website"},"mainEntity":[{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/hot-water-safety-checks/#article"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Check for a clean blue gas flame (not yellow or sooty), a relief valve that only discharges while heating (not constantly), and hot water that's warm but not scalding. Any warning sign on these, or a gas smell, means stop and call a licensed professional."},"name":"How do I know if my hot water system is safe?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes — a faulty or poorly ventilated gas system can produce carbon monoxide, which is colourless and odourless. Warning signs are a yellow or sooty flame, black marks around the unit, and headaches, nausea or dizziness when it's running. Treat these as an emergency and call a licensed gasfitter."},"name":"Can a gas hot water system cause carbon monoxide?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Don't ignite anything (no switches, flames or phones inside), turn off the gas at the meter if it's safe, ventilate and get everyone outside, then call your gas emergency line or a licensed gasfitter from outside. Don't go back in until it's cleared."},"name":"What should I do if I smell gas?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"The tempering valve, which blends water down to a safe maximum of 50°C at your bathroom taps, may have failed. It's a safety risk — switch to cold at the tap and book a licensed plumber to replace it urgently."},"name":"Why is my hot water suddenly scalding hot?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"A little discharge from the TPR valve's drain line while the system is heating is normal. Constant streaming, or the valve running non-stop, is a fault or a pressure problem and needs a licensed plumber."},"name":"Is it normal for the relief valve to drip?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Only looking and noticing — flame colour, relief-valve behaviour, tap temperature, and keeping the area clear and ventilated. records.jsonld: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@graph":[{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/hot-water-system-cost-guide-sydney/#webpage","@type":["WebPage","FAQPage"],"breadcrumb":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/hot-water-system-cost-guide-sydney/#breadcrumb"},"description":"What hot water systems cost in Sydney in 2026 — unit prices for gas, electric, solar and heat pump, plus typical installation costs and what drives them.","image":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/hot-water-system-cost-guide-sydney/#primaryimage"},"inLanguage":"en-AU","isPartOf":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/#website"},"mainEntity":[{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/hot-water-system-cost-guide-sydney/#article"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Installed in 2026: electric storage around $760–$2,850, gas around $1,150–$3,325, a heat pump around $2,850–$5,700 before rebates (roughly $2,100–$4,450 after), and solar around $3,325–$6,650. Your exact price depends on the size and your site."},"name":"How much does a hot water system cost in Sydney?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Supply-only is just the unit — commonly $1,025–$2,525 for a tank. records.jsonld: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@graph":[{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/how-long-do-hot-water-systems-last/#webpage","@type":["WebPage","FAQPage"],"breadcrumb":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/how-long-do-hot-water-systems-last/#breadcrumb"},"description":"How long hot water systems last by type — gas, electric, solar and heat pump — what shortens their life, and the signs it is time to replace yours.","image":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/how-long-do-hot-water-systems-last/#primaryimage"},"inLanguage":"en-AU","isPartOf":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/#website"},"mainEntity":[{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/resources/how-long-do-hot-water-systems-last/#article"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Between about 8 and 20 years depending on type: electric storage 8–12, gas storage 10–12, gas continuous flow 15–20, heat pump 10–15, and solar collectors 15–20 (with the tank 10–15). Care and water quality decide where yours lands."},"name":"How long do hot water systems last on average?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Gas continuous flow — with no tank to corrode, these commonly last 15–20 years. Solar collectors last a long time too, though their tank is on the shorter cycle."},"name":"Which hot water system lasts the longest?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Typically 8–12 years. Replacing the sacrificial anode during servicing — before it's fully spent, often around five years — is the single biggest thing that pushes it toward the top of that range."},"name":"How long does an electric hot water system last?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Hard or aggressive water, a spent anode left unreplaced, high mains pressure with no pressure limiting valve, and never servicing it. All of them are avoidable with a basic service schedule."},"name":"What shortens a hot water system's lifespan?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Rusty or discoloured water, leaks from the tank base, less hot water than before, rising bills and repeat repairs — especially on a system near the top of its age range."},"name":"How do I know my hot water system is near the end?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes, significantly — especially replacing the anode on a storage tank and keeping pressure in check. records.jsonld: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@graph":[{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/guides/pressure-limiting-valve/#webpage","@type":["WebPage","FAQPage"],"breadcrumb":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/guides/pressure-limiting-valve/#breadcrumb"},"description":"What a pressure limiting valve (PLV) does, why hot water systems need one, the signs it is failing, and when it has to be replaced. A plain-English guide.","image":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/guides/pressure-limiting-valve/#primaryimage"},"inLanguage":"en-AU","isPartOf":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/#website"},"mainEntity":[{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/guides/pressure-limiting-valve/#article"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"A pressure limiting valve (PLV) sits on the water supply to your hot water system and caps the incoming pressure at a safe level, protecting the tank, the fittings and every valve downstream from high or spiking mains pressure."},"name":"What is a pressure limiting valve?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"It automatically reduces incoming mains pressure to the rating it's set for and holds it there, so your hot water system only ever sees the pressure it was designed to handle — no adjustment needed from you."},"name":"How does a pressure limiting valve work?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"They're closely related and the terms are often used interchangeably on hot water installs — both cap and steady the incoming pressure. The key is that the valve is the correct rating for your system; a licensed plumber selects it."},"name":"Is a pressure limiting valve the same as a pressure reducing valve?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Parts of Sydney run mains pressure higher than a hot water system is rated for. Without a PLV, that pressure strains the tank and valves and forces water out of the relief valve. The PLV keeps everything working within its design pressure."},"name":"Why does my hot water system need a PLV?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Banging pipes, constant dripping from the relief valve, weeping fittings (pressure too high), or a noticeable drop in hot water flow (pressure too low or the valve clogged). Any of these is worth a pressure check."},"name":"What are the signs a PLV is failing?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"No — it's licensed plumbing work, and the valve has to be the correct pressure rating for your system and supply. A PLV replacement that's the wrong rating either fails to protect the system or starves the taps."},"name":"Can I replace a PLV myself?"}],"name":"Pressure Limiting Valves records.jsonld: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@graph":[{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/guides/tempering-valve/#webpage","@type":["WebPage","FAQPage"],"breadcrumb":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/guides/tempering-valve/#breadcrumb"},"description":"What a tempering valve does, why it is mandatory on storage hot water systems, how it keeps water safe at 50°C, and when it needs replacing. Simple guide.","image":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/guides/tempering-valve/#primaryimage"},"inLanguage":"en-AU","isPartOf":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/#website"},"mainEntity":[{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/guides/tempering-valve/#article"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"A tempering valve is a thermostatic blending valve on your hot water outlet. It mixes very hot stored water with cold to deliver a safe temperature (no more than 50°C) to your bathroom and hygiene taps, while the tank stays hot enough to kill bacteria."},"name":"What is a tempering valve?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Every time you run a hot tap, it automatically blends the water down to a safe, steady temperature. You never adjust it — it responds to the incoming hot and cold on its own."},"name":"What does a tempering valve do day to day?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"If you have a storage hot water system and taps used for bathing or washing, then yes — the plumbing code requires temperature-limited delivery and a tempering valve is the standard way to meet it. We fit a compliant valve as part of any storage system installation or replacement."},"name":"Do I need a tempering valve?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"The usual signs are water that's suddenly too hot (the dangerous one — treat it as urgent) or hot water that's gone lukewarm even though the tank is working. Both point to a valve that's no longer blending correctly and should be checked."},"name":"How do I know my tempering valve is failing?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"No. It sits on pressurised hot water, must be the correct rating, and has to be installed to code — so it's licensed plumbing work. Adjusting or bypassing one yourself can leave water dangerously hot. Book a licensed plumber."},"name":"Can I adjust or replace a tempering valve myself?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"They have a service life of around five years. We check it at every service and recommend replacing it at the first sign it isn't holding a safe, steady delivery temperature."},"name":"How often should a tempering valve be replaced?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"The valve itself is inexpensive; the price depends on access and how it's plumbed. We give you an exact figure after a quick look rather than a guess — and it's a fast job if we're already on site."},"name":"What does a tempering valve replacement cost?"}],"name":"Tempering Valves records.jsonld: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@graph":[{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/guides/tpr-valve/#webpage","@type":["WebPage","FAQPage"],"breadcrumb":{"@id":"https://sydneyhotwatersystems.com.au/guides/tpr-valve/#breadcrumb"},"description":"What a TPR (temperature & pressure relief) valve does on your hot water system, why it drips, how often to test it, and when to replace it. Storage systems are measured in litres (tank volume); continuous flow systems are measured by flow rate in litres per minute. You size storage to your peak draw, and continuous flow to how many outlets run at once."},"name":"How is hot water system size measured?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Because it only reheats overnight on the cheaper tariff, an off-peak electric tank has to hold a full day's hot water — so it's sized larger than a gas or continuous system that reheats any time."},"name":"Why does my electric off-peak tank need to be bigger?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You run out at peak — the classic cold shower when someone's already used the hot water. The goal is to size to your real peak demand with a sensible buffer, not to go as big as possible."},"name":"Is a bigger hot water system always better?"},{"@type":"Question","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes — sizing is part of every quote.
